findings.location: docs/papers/programmable-sovereignty/sections/03-substrate.tex L12 (paragraph 'Treaty scope and ladder')
findings.claim: The finite order is observation, guarded, receipt-backed, partition-contingency, and quorum-required. Intersection takes the stricter participant mode and rejects a destructive class below receipt-backed. An unknown class denies.
findings.evidence: spec/CHIO_LADDER.md L312-316: 'observation < guarded < receipt_backed < partition_contingency < maintenance' and L494 modes list ending in 'maintenance'. crates/kernel/chio-runtime-core/src/treaty.rs L752-763 ladder_mode_rank: observation 0, guarded 1, receipt_backed 2, partition_contingency 3, "maintenance" | "quorum_required" 4. crates/trust/chio-federation/src/treaty.rs L859-870 ladder_mode_rank: same but only "maintenance" at 4 (no quorum_required). bilateral_dsse_consistency_model L765-776 accepts "quorum-required" as a consistency model, not a mode. compute_ladder_intersection L364-368 takes max rank; L392-396 rejects destructive when mode_rank < rank(receipt_backed) with chio_ladder_destructive_below_floor; find_ladder_action None -> chio_treaty_action_class_not_allowed; validate_governance_ladder_manifest L129-134 requires default_unknown_mode == "deny". formal/proof-manifest.toml L1120-1139 mirrors only the chio-runtime-core copy of ladder_mode_rank.
findings.truth_at_head: The five ladder modes in the spec and in Rust are observation, guarded, receipt_backed, partition_contingency, maintenance. 'quorum-required' (hyphen) is a consistency_model value, never a mode. chio-runtime-core additionally tolerates the spelling 'quorum_required' as an alias of maintenance (rank 4); chio-federation rejects it, so the two ladder_mode_rank implementations diverge on that input. The stricter-mode, receipt_backed destructive floor, and unknown-class-denies rules are implemented as the paper says.
findings.recommended_fix: Replace 'quorum-required' with 'maintenance' in section 3 (and anywhere else the ladder is listed); optionally note that quorum requirements are expressed through consistency_model/co_sign, not a ladder mode. Separately, reconcile the two Rust ladder_mode_rank copies (drop or propagate the quorum_required alias) so the mirror-hashed runtime-core version is the only semantics.
findings.verifier_evidence: Read 03-substrate.tex L12; CHIO_LADDER.md L305-320, L488-500 and grep for quorum (L258, L289, L430: consistency_model only); both schema $defs.mode enums; runtime-core treaty.rs ladder_mode_rank L752-763 and bilateral_dsse_consistency_model L765-776; federation treaty.rs ladder_mode_rank L859-870 and validate_consistency_model L873-875; compute_ladder_intersection L355-400; validate_governance_ladder_manifest L120-140; proof-manifest.toml L1120-1139; PredicateLang.lean L18-40.
findings.adjustment: The quoted sentence is at sections/03-substrate.tex L12 verbatim. The fifth mode in the spec of record (spec/CHIO_LADDER.md L311-313 and L494), in both JSON schemas (spec/schemas/chio-federation/v1/governance-ladder-manifest.schema.json L36-44; ladder-intersection.schema.json L43-51), and in chio-federation's ladder_mode_rank (crates/trust/chio-federation/src/treaty.rs L859-870) is 'maintenance'; chio-federation rejects 'quorum_required' with chio_federation_ladder_invalid_mode. 'quorum-required' (hyphen) is a consistency_model enum value in the spec and both Rust validators. The correction to the finding: the paper's word is not invented; it is the vocabulary of the Lean abstraction anchor (formal/lean4/Chio/Chio/Treaty/PredicateLang.lean L20-34: TrustMode = observation, guarded, receiptBacked, partitionContingency, quorumRequired with rank 4, docstring 'Ordered governance modes accepted by the production ladder parser') and of the runtime-core alias ('maintenance' | 'quorum_required' => 4, crates/kernel/chio-runtime-core/src/treaty.rs L752-763), which proof-manifest.toml L1120-1139 mirrors. So the divergence is three-way: spec/schema/federation say maintenance; runtime-core accepts both spellings; Lean and the paper say quorumRequired. The paper should follow the spec, and the Lean docstring is also inaccurate for chio-federation. Stricter-mode (treaty.rs L356-359), receipt_backed destructive floor (L380-385, chio_ladder_destructive_below_floor) and default_unknown_mode == deny (L133-138) are implemented as claimed.

findings.location: docs/papers/programmable-sovereignty/sections/05-implementation.tex L92-93 ('Runtime and Offline Review'); also 06-evaluation.tex L60-62
findings.claim: The negative matrix calls the same public verification surfaces. Envelope cases call the strict verifier; store and policy cases call the admission hook.
findings.evidence: examples/chio-3vendor/fixtures/treaty-runtime-negative-corpus.json maps each threatId to a testFilter. PS-TH-01 -> runtime_treaty.rs L355 bounded_treaty_view_binds_runtime_artifacts_and_rejects_wrong_treaty, which calls bounded_treaty_receipt_view_from_verified_artifacts (predicate.rs L218) and emits err.code() at L565. PS-TH-02 (L895) and PS-TH-03 (L1108) call evaluate_cross_boundary_admission directly. PS-TH-13 (bilateral_verifier/tests.rs L1195-1218), PS-TH-14 (L1283-1306) and PS-TH-19 (L1221-1280) call verify_bilateral_cosign_invocation, defined at cosign.rs L500 with the doc comment 'Partial-verifier scope: this is a partial local verifier ... but is not full section 7 conformance: predicate schema fields are missing (e.g. tool_args_hash)'. PS-TH-05/06/07 call verify_chio_bilateral_invocation (tests.rs L646-745). PS-TH-08/09/10/11/12/18 are bilateral_dsse::tests envelope/signer tests. PS-TH-04/15/16/17/20 call ChioRuntimeAdmissionHook::evaluate.
findings.truth_at_head: Of the 20 cases: 5 call the admission hook (04, 15, 16, 17, 20); 3 call the strict operational verifier verify_chio_bilateral_invocation (05, 06, 07); 6 call the bilateral_dsse envelope verifier or signer (08, 09, 10, 11, 12, 18); 3 call the partial legacy verifier verify_bilateral_cosign_invocation (13, 14, 19); and 3 call neither the hook nor any DSSE verifier but pure runtime-core functions bounded_treaty_receipt_view_from_verified_artifacts (01) and evaluate_cross_boundary_admission (02, 03). The wrong-treaty attack (PS-TH-01) is thus evidenced by the bounded predicate library's constructor, which section 5 says 'does not grant access on behalf of the admission hook'; the hook does enforce chio_treaty_scope_hash_mismatch itself (admission_hook/treaty_evidence.rs L36-41) but no matrix case exercises that path.
findings.recommended_fix: State the real split in section 5/6 (hook, strict operational verifier, envelope verifier, partial verifier, pure validators), or retarget PS-TH-01..03 to hook-level tests (e.g. a treatyScopeSha256 mismatch through ChioRuntimeAdmissionHook::evaluate) and PS-TH-13/14/19 to verify_chio_bilateral_invocation so that the sentence becomes true.
findings.verifier_evidence: Parsed examples/chio-3vendor/fixtures/treaty-runtime-negative-corpus.json (20 cases, testFilter per case); located every test fn by grep and read each body's verification call and emit_threat_matrix_code site; read cosign.rs L489-505 doc comment ('Partial-verifier scope'); read verify.rs L17-60 and L150-200; read PREDICATE_TYPE_BILATERAL / PREDICATE_TYPE_CHIO_BILATERAL_INVOCATION in types.rs L16-19.

Section 6 L61 ('stop at the validator or admission hook') partly concedes this, but section 5 L92-93 as quoted is false at HEAD: no matrix case reaches the hook's chio_treaty_scope_hash_mismatch path (admission_hook/treaty_evidence.rs), and 'Envelope cases call the strict verifier' is wrong for 08/11/12/18 as well as for 13/14/19.

findings.location: docs/papers/programmable-sovereignty/sections/05-implementation.tex L4-10 and L32-48 ('Bilateral Statement'); 03-substrate.tex L44 (step 4) and L46 (step 6)
findings.claim: It then compares the authenticated values with receiver-owned state: peer pins, live manifests, the revocation epoch, receipt signatures and hashes, the capability lease, policy results, and required governance evidence.
findings.evidence: grep of production callers: verify_chio_bilateral_invocation is called only from crates/trust/chio-attest-buyer-core/src/report.rs L266 (offline verify_package). The pre-dispatch hook calls chio_federation::bilateral_dsse::verify_chio_bilateral_dsse_envelope at crates/kernel/chio-runtime-core/src/admission_hook/dsse.rs L121 after its own checks (predicate_type L19-26, validate_policy_evaluation_summary + server_a_verdict == allow L27-44, treaty_binding_ref field equality vs stored scope/intersection/continuation/request L52-64, tool_args_hash L65-76, lease_refs == bundle.lease_id L77-82, governance_refs == bundle.governance_receipt_id L83-95, signer set == treaty participants L96-110, distinct participant keys L111-119). chio-kernel verified_treaty.rs L71 also calls verify_chio_bilateral_dsse_envelope and checks capability_lease_ref.expires_at_unix_ms against now (L136-145). Peer pin set, require_fresh_ladder_manifest, revocation_oracle.is_active_at_epoch, receipt_store.resolve + verify_signature, lease_registry.resolve and governance_receipt_store exist only in bilateral_verifier/cosign.rs L104-350 (verify_chio_bilateral_invocation_inner). No 'revocation' or 'pin' reference exists in admission_hook.rs or admission_hook/{treaty_ref,treaty_evidence,dsse}.rs (grep).
findings.truth_at_head: The receiver's pre-dispatch path is: kernel checks -> ChioRuntimeAdmissionHook::evaluate -> verify_treaty_reference_from_store (continuation window/binding, lineage bundle, bilateral invocation binding, DSSE binding checks, verify_chio_bilateral_dsse_envelope) -> evaluate_cross_boundary_admission -> VerifiedFederationTreatyMaterial::verify (re-verifies the envelope, lease expiry from the predicate's own lease ref, policy allow, admission binding) -> consume continuation -> evaluate_runtime_admission_tracked. That path never consults a PeerPinSet, ladder-manifest freshness, a revocation oracle at an epoch, a lease registry, a governance receipt store, or a resolved receipt's signature; participant keys come from the stored TreatyScope, and lease/governance checks are string-equality against the stored admission bundle. verify_chio_bilateral_invocation with those checks runs only in the offline buyer package verifier (verify_package). The paper's Table 1 attribution (federation tests and matrix) is accurate; its placement in the receiver control flow and the step-4/step-6 check lists are not.
findings.recommended_fix: In section 5 name verify_chio_bilateral_dsse_envelope plus admission_hook/dsse.rs and VerifiedFederationTreatyMaterial::verify as the pre-dispatch verifiers and list exactly what they check; move verify_chio_bilateral_invocation (peer pins, ladder-manifest freshness, revocation epoch, receipt store, lease registry, governance store) to the offline review subsection. Amend section 3 steps 4 and 6 accordingly, or add the missing lookups to the hook.
findings.verifier_evidence: Quoted sentence is at 05-implementation.tex L42-44 verbatim; steps 4 and 6 at 03-substrate.tex L44 and L46. grep: the only non-test caller of verify_chio_bilateral_invocation is crates/trust/chio-attest-buyer-core/src/report.rs L266 (offline verify_package). The hook's DSSE check is admission_hook/dsse.rs L7-140: predicate type (L19-26), validate_policy_evaluation_summary plus server_a_verdict == allow only (L27-44), treaty_binding_ref field equality vs stored scope/intersection/continuation/action/consistency/request (L52-64), tool_args_hash (L65-76), lease_refs string-equal to bundle.lease_id (L77-82), governance_refs string-equal to bundle.governance_receipt_id (L83-95), signer set == participants (L96-110), distinct keys (L111-119), verify_chio_bilateral_dsse_envelope (L121-129), lineage hash equality (L130-140). No peer_pin, revocation, is_active_at_epoch or require_fresh_ladder_manifest string exists in admission_hook.rs or admission_hook/{treaty_ref,treaty_evidence,dsse,store_artifacts}.rs (the only 'revocation' hits are swarm_ref.rs/swarm_authority.rs, the swarm path). Those lookups exist only in bilateral_verifier/cosign.rs verify_chio_bilateral_invocation_inner (peer_pin_set L67/L84, require_fresh_ladder_manifest L118-119, revocation_oracle.is_active_at_epoch L121/L130, receipt_store.resolve L142 + verify_signature L151, lease_registry.resolve L249, governance_receipt_store L323/L340). Hook order confirmed: verify_treaty_reference_from_store (admission_hook.rs L795) -> evaluate_cross_boundary_admission (treaty_evidence.rs L225) -> VerifiedFederationTreatyMaterial::verify (treaty_evidence.rs L278; verified_treaty.rs L71 re-verifies envelope, L133-145 lease expiry from the predicate's own capability_lease_ref against now) -> consume_treaty_continuation (L836) -> evaluate_runtime_admission_tracked (L947). The hook path never calls verify_signature on a resolved receipt; treaty_evidence.rs only checks lineage-bundle hash bindings (L348-424).

findings.truth_at_head: The manifest is intact except for two workspace-level files unrelated to the paper's content: Cargo.lock and rust-toolchain.toml. Every paper section, figure, script, result file, corpus, Lean source, diff-test source and named Rust source file still matches its recorded sha256, and the recorded benchmark provenance digests still verify because they are computed on git trees at fixed commits. findings.location: docs/papers/programmable-sovereignty/sections/05-implementation.tex L16-20; 03-substrate.tex L43 (step 3)
findings.claim: \codepath{treaty_ref_from_request} rejects request-carried trust roots, peer directories, signing keys, revocation records, and dynamic trust bundles.
findings.evidence: crates/kernel/chio-runtime-core/src/admission_hook/treaty_ref.rs L38-60: denylist trustRoot, trustRoots, trustBundle, treatyScope, ladderManifest, signingKey, peerDirectory -> request_smuggled_trust_root; dynamicTrust, dynamicTrustBundle, runtimeTrustInput, peerDiscovery -> request_smuggled_dynamic_trust. No key naming revocation records. The scan covers only governed_intent.context.chioTreaty (L26-37). Everything else read from the request is an identifier or sha256 (L61-117); store_artifacts.rs and treaty_evidence.rs resolve all artifacts from RuntimeAdmissionStore by those identifiers. Tests runtime_admission.rs L518-556 and L558-596 insert trustRoot / dynamicTrust into the chioTreaty object.
findings.truth_at_head: Request metadata cannot install a trust root because the hook only ever reads identifiers and hashes from the chioTreaty object and resolves every artifact from its own store; the denylist is a defense-in-depth check on eleven specific key names inside chioTreaty. It contains no revocation-record key, and unknown keys inside chioTreaty (or trust-shaped keys elsewhere in the context) are ignored rather than denied.
findings.recommended_fix: Drop 'revocation records' from the list (or add a revocation key to the denylist), and state that the structural guarantee comes from identifier-only parsing plus store resolution, with the denylist as an explicit-rejection layer for the named keys.
findings.verifier_evidence: 05-implementation.tex L17-18 reads exactly as quoted; 03-substrate.tex L43 lists 'trust root, peer directory, signing key, or dynamic trust bundle' (no revocation there). crates/kernel/chio-runtime-core/src/admission_hook/treaty_ref.rs L38-60: seven keys (trustRoot, trustRoots, trustBundle, treatyScope, ladderManifest, signingKey, peerDirectory) -> request_smuggled_trust_root; four keys (dynamicTrust, dynamicTrustBundle, runtimeTrustInput, peerDiscovery) -> request_smuggled_dynamic_trust; eleven keys total, none naming revocation. The scan is limited to governed_intent.context.chioTreaty (L26-37); everything else read is an identifier or sha256 (L61-117) and artifacts are resolved from RuntimeAdmissionStore. Unknown keys inside chioTreaty are ignored.

findings.location: docs/papers/programmable-sovereignty/sections/05-implementation.tex L25-28; 03-substrate.tex L15; CLAIM_LEDGER.md L14
findings.claim: The hook reserves the continuation while admission is in progress, consumes it before an admitted dispatch, and releases it after a pre-dispatch denial or abort.
findings.evidence: admission_hook.rs L833-871: after verify_treaty_reference_from_store succeeds, evaluate calls store.consume_treaty_continuation(continuation_id, admission_id) before evaluate_runtime_admission_tracked (L940); a Rejected error there yields chio_treaty_continuation_replay. On a non-accepted runtime report (L1024-1064) it calls release_reservations, which invokes store.release_treaty_continuation. On accept it writes reserved_treaty_continuation_id into metadata (L1008-1011); the kernel calls hook.release_reserved on pre-dispatch denial (dispatch.rs L1644-1680). RuntimeAdmissionStore has only consume_* and release_* (no reserve or mark-consumed). SQLite (store/sqlite/admission_replay.rs L121-141): INSERT OR IGNORE into runtime_consumed_treaty_continuations (continuation_id, admission_id); 0 rows inserted -> replay; release L142-156 DELETE WHERE continuation_id AND admission_id. JSON store (store/json.rs L304-338) keeps a consumed_treaty_continuation_ids list keyed by continuation_id only. revalidate_admitted_request (L519-534) only compares the metadata's reserved_treaty_continuation_id with the request's continuation; it does not re-check the store. Tests treaty_runtime_hook_denies_replayed_continuation (L918), treaty_runtime_hook_releases_continuation_after_runtime_denial (L965), treaty_runtime_hook_releases_reserved_state_after_kernel_abort (L1016) exercise exactly this.
findings.truth_at_head: There is one consuming store operation, performed during admission (before the runtime policy step), and one releasing operation performed on runtime denial or on kernel pre-dispatch abort. An admitted continuation is never touched again; there is no second 'consume before dispatch' transition and no reserved-vs-consumed state in either store. Replay denial and release-then-readmit behave as the ledger row says.
findings.recommended_fix: Describe the lifecycle as 'consumed at admission, released on denial or pre-dispatch abort' (naming consume_treaty_continuation / release_treaty_continuation), and note that dispatch-time revalidation checks metadata consistency rather than store state.

findings.recommended_fix: Say what a sample is, or switch the deny/append benches to per-invocation timing (Criterion flat sampling or a hand-rolled loop recording each evaluation) and report percentiles of that distribution.

findings.evidence: Issues #1005-#1010 (all OPEN, lane lean-mutants, commit 0bb89a09) record six surviving mutants in PredicateLang.lean: `defined` L246 `.top => true`->false, L247 `.bot => true`->false, L249 `.disj` `&&`->`||`; `supported` L231 `.top`->false, L232 `.bot`->false, L234 `.disj` `&&`->`||`. Those line numbers match HEAD exactly (cat -n). formal/lean4/lean-mutants-allowlist.toml targets supported, defined, denote, refinesOnConstitution, ofDecide in the Treaty lane; ReceiptPredicate (P1's model) is not targeted at all. Scratch scratchpad/mutant_1007.lean at HEAD: with only the #1007 mutation (defined disj `||`) applied to a local copy, `denote (.neg (.disj (.atom (.modeAtLeast .receiptBacked)) .bot)) {acceptedAdmission with resolvedMode := none}` = false in the real model and = true under the mutant; both `example ... := by decide` succeeded and `#eval` printed `(false, true)`. The only theorems touching this shape are negated_unknown_atom_denies (L296-299, bare atom, `rfl`) and negated_unknown_mode_denies (L301-305, bare atom). A scratch theorem `defined_implies_supported` (structural induction) compiled, proving survivor #1010 is semantically equivalent w.r.t. denote (so it can only be killed by a definition-pinning lemma). Survivors #1005/#1006/#1008/#1009 make `denote .top view = false`; no theorem states top is admitted. The retained Lean report (target/formal/lean-mutants/report.json) is not in the repo; only the issues and CURRENT_STATE.md record the campaign (45 mutants, 33 killed, 12 survivors, 73.3 percent).
findings.truth_at_head: The Treaty theorem set does not pin the `.top`, `.bot`, or `.disj` cases of `supported`/`defined`. The conj case is pinned only incidentally (accept_conj_scope_decompose's simp uses it, which is why conj mutants died). Under a single surviving mutant (#1007) the design goal stated in the file header is violated for the shape neg (disj undefinedAtom bot), and no theorem detects it. This is the `denote` that P2's third conjunct calls, so P2's 'fail-closed scope denotation' rests on a definition whose fail-closed propagation through disjunction is unproved. P1 is unaffected (different module) but has zero mutation evidence.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a structural theorem such as `containsUndefinedAtom p view = true → denote p view = false` (and the supported analogue) proved by induction over Predicate; this kills #1005-#1009 and turns the header's prose claim into a theorem. Dispose #1010 as an equivalent mutant with the `defined_implies_supported` lemma. Retain the Lean mutation report under formal/mutation/evidence/ like the Rust and TLA+ lanes. P2 should not describe the scope conjunct as fail-closed beyond what is proved for bare atoms.
findings.verifier_evidence: Reproduced at HEAD with scratchpad/verify/mutant_v.lean (compiles, exit 0): with only the #1007 mutation (defined .disj using ||) applied to a local copy, `denote (.neg (.disj (.atom (.modeAtLeast .receiptBacked)) .bot)) {acceptedAdmission with resolvedMode := none}` evaluates to false in the real model and true under the mutant (#eval printed (false, true); both `by decide` examples pass). `defined_implies_supported` proved by structural induction, so #1010 is denote-equivalent. A defined-with-top=false variant makes denote .top = false, and grep shows no theorem in Treaty/*.lean mentions `.top`. Issues #1005-#1010 are OPEN, lane lean-mutants, commit 0bb89a09, and their line numbers (231, 232, 234, 246, 247, 249) match HEAD. lean-mutants-allowlist.toml targets supported/defined/denote/refinesOnConstitution/ofDecide only; no ReceiptPredicate entry. However the fail-closed claim is PredicateLang.lean's header (L11-13), not a paper claim: grep of P2 for 'fail-closed', 'unsupported atom', 'signer_alias' hits only 01 L13 (the hook fails closed) and P1 uses ReceiptPredicate, which has no supported/defined layer. The gap is already tracked in open issues and CURRENT_STATE.md L36-42.
findings.adjustment: Repo formal weakness, confirmed by reproduction: no Treaty theorem pins the .top/.bot/.disj cases of supported/defined, so under tracked survivor #1007 the header's 'unsupported atom cannot be turned into an allow decision by wrapping it in neg' is violated for neg (disj undefinedAtom bot) without any theorem failing. Neither paper asserts fail-closed denotation, and the survivors are already recorded in open issues #1005-#1010 and CURRENT_STATE.md, so for the papers this is a note-level caution (do not add a fail-closed claim to P2 without the structural theorem); for the formal lane it is a real, acknowledged gap.

Shallow list lemmas: finite_refinement_sound/exact (P1), refinesOn_complete_on_fragment, refinesOnConstitution_complete_on_fragment (+ alias refinesOnConstitution_iff), atom_constitution_exact and runtime_admission_policy_exact (List.all over map), bridge_refinement_on_iff / bridge_global_iff / bridge_soundness / bridge_decidable_soundness. Genuine induction: bridge_pointwise (induction on the predicate list, trivial step), essential_preserved_chain / containsPredicate_preserved_chain (Nat induction with the step supplied as hypothesis). Most substantive: ConstitutionalDeltaSyn.ofDecide_isSome_iff (dependent-witness constructor iff Prop; by_cases + simp) and Legacy.amendment_admissible_iff_backward_refinement (extracts a proof term from a record).
findings.truth_at_head: Of the 52 theorems in the lane (4+2+23+4+9+4+12 minus re-export overlap), none establishes a non-trivial invariant; the security-relevant content is the fail-closed family (unsupported/undefined/negated_* and signer_*), all of which are hypothesis-form or bare-atom statements and none of which pins the propagation of supported/defined through disj/top/bot (FORM-08). What would materially strengthen a paper: (a) a structural fail-closed theorem over arbitrary predicates, (b) ofDecide_isSome_iff as the amendment decision procedure statement, (c) runtime_admission_policy_exact together with the mirror anchors as the bounded model of the actual Rust gate list (12 atoms at L382-395). What would not: the anchor lane, the tautologies, the reassociation lemmas, and the closure bridge (model-to-model only). Neither paper cites signer_alias_reuse_denies although it is the Lean form of P2's signer-reuse gate; P2 instead declares signer distinctness 'assumed-sound' outside Lean (04 L13).
findings.recommended_fix: Papers should cite the fail-closed family and runtime_admission_policy_exact with the mirror anchors if they want a formal story about the runtime gate list, and should stop citing tautologies and rfl lemmas as theorems. findings.claim: Third, on any denial or aborted continuation, reserved kernel state is released back to free, so that an attacker watching a continuation get admitted then aborted cannot replay it under a fresh request.
findings.evidence: crates/kernel/chio-kernel/src/kernel/dispatch.rs L1644-1677 release_runtime_admission_reservations_for_pre_dispatch_denial: on hook.release_reserved error it returns metadata {reservation_release_failed: true, reservation_retained: true} and false. crates/kernel/chio-runtime-core/src/admission_hook.rs L833-871: consume_treaty_continuation Err (non-Rejected) or panic returns a deny with 'ambiguous_treaty_continuation_id' metadata and does not release; L609-628 release_reserved wraps the store call in catch_unwind and reports failures. formal/apalache/PostAdmissionDropGuard.tla header: 'A release error or panic is projected as retained or possibly stuck, and the concrete callback is not retried.' formal/MAPPING.md row RetainedIffAborted maps to ChioKernel::mark_runtime_admission_reservations_retained_fail_closed and ChioRuntimeAdmissionHook::release_reserved.
findings.truth_at_head: Release is best-effort. On a release error, panic, or ambiguous consumption, the kernel retains the reservation fail-closed (the continuation stays consumed) and records it in the denial receipt metadata. findings.recommended_fix: Rewrite as: on pre-dispatch denial the hook attempts to release the continuation; if release fails or consumption is ambiguous the reservation is retained fail-closed and named in the denial metadata. Cite PostAdmissionDropGuard.tla RetainedIffAborted and the drop_guard_disposition_table proptest as the evidence.

findings.evidence: The five-code taxonomy is repeated in the abstract, contribution bullet 1, the accept-set paragraph, fig:gates, tab:rejection-codes, the evaluation ('every disagreement is named by exactly one rejection code', 06 L22), the error-oracle attack (07 L34) and README.md. Ground truth item 8: VerifierError (crates/trust/chio-federation/src/bilateral_verifier/error.rs) has 16 codes; BilateralCoSigningError::code adds 8 more; the negative corpus maps the paper's 'noncanonical-payload' case to statement.malformed, 'wrong-predicate-type' to predicate.type_unrecognised, 'repeated-signer-key' to signer.independence_required, 'stale-lease' to capability.lease_expired_or_unknown, and receipt/request/outcome mismatch to predicate.schema_invalid (examples/chio-3vendor/fixtures/treaty-runtime-negative-corpus.json).
findings.truth_at_head: No code named noncanonical-payload, predicate-type-mismatch, signer-reuse, stale-lease or subject-digest-mismatch exists. The shipped taxonomy has 16 VerifierError codes plus BilateralCoSigningError codes, and most structural envelope failures are BilateralCoSigningError::CanonicalJson(String) distinguished by message prefix. The paper's central structural claim (one code per gate, five gates) is not a description of the artifact.
findings.recommended_fix: Rewrite the paper around the real 16-code VerifierError taxonomy (or the spec's 15 codes in spec/CHIO_BILATERAL_COSIGN_INVOCATION.md section 7.1), regenerate fig:gates and tab:rejection-codes from error.rs, and drop every 'five' in abstract, intro, README and title-level framing.

findings.claim: The finite order is observation, guarded, receipt-backed, partition-contingency, and quorum-required.
findings.evidence: crates/trust/chio-federation/src/treaty.rs L859-871 fn ladder_mode_rank: observation=0, guarded=1, receipt_backed=2, partition_contingency=3, maintenance=4, anything else rejected with chio_federation_ladder_invalid_mode. crates/kernel/chio-runtime-core/src/treaty.rs L752 has the same function. spec/CHIO_LADDER.md L313-314: 'observation < guarded < receipt_backed < partition_contingency < maintenance'. 'quorum-required' is a consistency_model enum value (spec/CHIO_LADDER.md L258, L430) and appears in Rust only as consistency_model strings (frost/registry.rs L49 onward, bilateral_verifier/tests.rs L719).
findings.truth_at_head: The fifth and strictest ladder mode is maintenance. quorum-required is a consistency model, a different axis of the same manifest. Both mirror hashes for ladder_mode_rank are registered in formal/proof-manifest.toml, so the paper misnames a proof-linked constant.
findings.recommended_fix: Change the sentence to 'observation, guarded, receipt-backed, partition-contingency, and maintenance' and, if the paper wants to mention quorum-required, introduce it as a consistency-model value in the same paragraph that introduces consistency models.
findings.verifier_evidence: Federation treaty.rs L859-871; runtime-core treaty.rs L752-764 and L770 ('quorum_required' | 'quorum-required' => 'quorum-required' consistency model), L785 (co_sign alias to n_of_m); spec/CHIO_LADDER.md L258 consistency_model enum includes quorum-required, L313-314 mode order ends in maintenance; proof-manifest.toml L1120-1140 single mirror block.
findings.adjustment: P1 03 L12 names the fifth ladder mode 'quorum-required'; the normative spec (spec/CHIO_LADDER.md L313-314, L494) and the federation crate (crates/trust/chio-federation/src/treaty.rs L859-871 ladder_mode_rank: observation 0, guarded 1, receipt_backed 2, partition_contingency 3, maintenance 4, else chio_federation_ladder_invalid_mode) name it 'maintenance'. However the finder is wrong that runtime-core 'has the same function' and that quorum-required 'appears in Rust only as consistency_model strings': crates/kernel/chio-runtime-core/src/treaty.rs L752-764 accepts '"maintenance" | "quorum_required" => Ok(4)', i.e. the underscore spelling is an accepted legacy alias at the same rank, exercised by tests/runtime_treaty.rs L33/L55. Only one [[mirror]] block registers ladder_mode_rank (formal/proof-manifest.toml L1120-1140, rust_source = runtime-core treaty.rs), not 'both'. So the paper's name is an imprecise legacy alias rather than a false statement about the runtime it describes; the canonical name is maintenance and the hyphenated 'quorum-required' is a consistency_model value.

findings.claim: The adversary learns which conjunct failed, not which byte disagreed, which keyid was reused, or which scope component diverged.

findings.truth_at_head: The shipped verifier's errors carry the offending field values in their message strings, so the 'coarse conjunct-only' error surface the paper credits with defeating error-message oracles is not what the code emits. findings.location: paper.tex L39 (abstract); sections/01-introduction.tex L15; sections/07-attacks-defeated.tex L26, L32, L36, L38; sections/06-evaluation.tex L20
findings.claim: Six classes of attack against cross-organizational receipt evidence are rejected structurally rather than detected.
findings.evidence: The abstract names three defeated attacks; contribution bullet 4 names four ('sibling-treaty cross-receipt substitution, BBS stub-vs-real disambiguation, single-lane witness compromise, and error-message oracles are rejected by construction'); section 7 opens with six. Of the six, 'Schema-version downgrade' says 'Multi-version coexistence ... is out of scope for this primitive' (L36) and 'Constitutional ratchet' says 'This is out of scope at the envelope layer' (L38). 'Single-lane witness compromise' has no evaluation: section 6 L20 says 'Anchor-inclusion latency across the Rekor, OpenTimestamps, Solana memo, and EVM event lanes is also unmeasured here', and ground truth item 11 leaves the existence of a treaty-bound multi-lane witness policy in Rust unverified.
findings.truth_at_head: The paper gives three different counts for the same claim, two of the six 'defeated' classes are declared out of scope in their own paragraphs, and one is evidenced nowhere in the paper. The anchor lanes (bitcoin.rs, evm.rs, solana.rs, witness.rs, rekor, opentimestamps in crates/economy/chio-anchor) exist, but no fixture or test in the paper exercises them.
findings.recommended_fix: Pick one list, keep only classes that have a named fixture or test in section 6, move the two out-of-scope classes to Limitations, and either evaluate single-lane compromise against a named anchor-policy test or remove it from the contributions.
findings.verifier_evidence: Abstract (paper.tex L39) names three; 01 L15 names four; 07 L4 'Six classes'. 07 L14 (schema-version): 'Multi-version coexistence during a deployment migration window is out of scope for this primitive'; 07 L16 (ratchet): 'This is out of scope at the envelope layer'. 06 L20: anchor-inclusion latency 'unmeasured here'. findings.truth_at_head: Missing references a PC will raise, one line each: PolicyMaker/KeyNote (Blaze-Feigenbaum-Lacy 1996) is the original 'compliance checking of credentials against local policy', i.e. receiver-owned admission by another name; SDSI/SPKI (Rivest-Lampson; RFC 2693) introduced receiver-local naming and authorization certificates and is the ancestor of 'trust resolved from the receiver's own stores'; Macaroons (Birgisson et al. 2014) and Biscuit are attenuable bearer tokens with contextual caveats, the obvious alternative to treaty-bound predicates; UCAN and ZCAP-LD are the capability-token formats agent frameworks actually use; SPIFFE/SPIRE federation solves cross-organization trust-bundle exchange in production and is the deployed answer to 'who provisions the receiver's peer pins'; RFC 8693 token exchange and OAuth actor claims are the standards-track cross-domain delegation story; W3C VC/VP with BBS is the closest existing 'selective disclosure at presentation' design (P2 section 2.4); SCITT/COSE receipts and CT/Trillian are the transparency comparators P1 omits though it targets USENIX; Kerberos cross-realm is the canonical two-administrative-domain key-trust system; BeyondCorp is per-request verification against receiver-owned state; AWS cross-account resource policies and SCPs are receiver-side evaluation of foreign principals at scale; Zanzibar/OPA are the policy-engine comparators for 'receiver policy accepts?'; CHERI and the WebAssembly component model are the current capability-enforcement substrates; MCP and A2A are the wire protocols agent tool calls actually cross, and the repo already integrates both; x402/AP2 are the agent-payment rails the buyer/vendor/refund framing implies.

findings.location: docs/papers/bilateral-receipt-admission/sections/09-limitations.tex L16
findings.claim: the wire format does not currently version-tag for cipher-suite agility, and adding such a tag (so a verifier can distinguish a v1 Ed25519/SHA-256 envelope from a successor profile without ambiguity) is part of the cryptographic-rotation work
findings.evidence: crates/trust/chio-federation/src/bilateral_dsse/types.rs L113-121: pub struct KernelIdentity { kernel_id, passport_key_fingerprint, alg: String } with deny_unknown_fields; spec/CHIO_BILATERAL_COSIGN_INVOCATION.md L294 'required: [kernel_id, passport_key_fingerprint, alg]' and L194-247 HashRecord 'alg' enum [sha256]; bilateral_dsse/verify.rs L296-299 and L524-527 reject tool_server_a/b.alg != 'ed25519', L637-639 reject record.alg != 'sha256' ('predicate.schema_invalid: {field}.alg must be sha256'); predicateType string 'chio.bilateral-cosign-invocation.v1' is itself versioned; chio-core-types receipt/body.rs L96-101 ChioReceipt.algorithm: Option<SigningAlgorithm>. The 03-p2 audit noted the alg tag inside IMPL2-29's truth text but no finding anchors on 09 L16.
findings.truth_at_head: The wire format carries and enforces per-signer algorithm tags (KernelIdentity.alg, must equal 'ed25519'), per-hash algorithm tags (HashRecord.alg, must equal 'sha256'), a versioned predicateType, and an optional receipt-level SigningAlgorithm. What is absent is a single envelope-level cipher-suite identifier; a successor profile would be distinguished today by predicateType and by the alg values the verifier refuses.
findings.recommended_fix: Replace the sentence with: 'Each kernel identity and hash record carries an alg tag that the verifier pins to ed25519 and sha256, and the predicate type is versioned; there is no single envelope-level suite identifier, so a successor suite would be introduced by a new predicateType plus new alg values.'

findings.location: P2 sections/03-predicate-schema-verifier.tex L72; P1 sections/09-limitations.tex L15-17 (tab:assumptions) and sections/02-background.tex L22
findings.claim: The JCS rules force deterministic key ordering, minimal numeric form, and Unicode string normalization, so two implementations that agree on the input fields produce byte-identical encodings. ... Canonical JSON matches RFC~8785
findings.evidence: crates/core/chio-core-types/src/canonical.rs (never opened by any prior finder): L8-12 doc states RFC 8785; L219-222 write_canonical_object sorts by cmp_utf16_code_units (L251-267); L268-283 canonicalize_number renders i64/u64 as exact decimal integers before falling back to canonicalize_f64 (L284-330: ryu shortest, exponent outside [1e-6,1e21), -0 to 0); escape_json_string (L342-362) escapes quotes, reverse solidus, and C0 controls only and performs no Unicode normalization (grep -i nfc|normaliz returns only the '-0' comment); only the strict text path canonical_json_bytes_from_str (L131-181) enforces the I-JSON 2^53-1 range and rejects duplicate keys and over-precise fractions, while the typed path canonical_json_bytes (L119-123) used for signing Rust values does not. formal/assumptions.toml L26 ASSUME-CANONICAL-JSON: 'Float rendering and float-bearing compound receipt fields outside that domain remain assumed deterministic and byte-stable'.
findings.truth_at_head: The production canonicalizer implements RFC 8785 key ordering, ECMAScript-style shortest double rendering, and JCS escaping, and neither RFC 8785 nor the implementation performs Unicode normalization (P2's 'Unicode string normalization' is not a JCS property). One divergence from a strict JCS reading exists on the typed path: u64/i64 magnitudes above 2^53-1 are emitted as exact integers rather than as IEEE-754 doubles, and only the untrusted-text entry point enforces the I-JSON range. The repository records the residual as audited assumption ASSUME-CANONICAL-JSON, which neither paper cites.
findings.recommended_fix: P2: delete 'Unicode string normalization' (JCS escapes, it does not normalize). P1 tab:assumptions: cite the implementation (chio-core-types canonical.rs) and formal/assumptions.toml ASSUME-CANONICAL-JSON, and note that signed payloads are integer-only structures within the I-JSON range so the float and large-integer residual does not reach the bilateral predicate.

critic_summary:
COMPLETENESS VERDICT. The seven finder/verifier reports (docs/papers/review-2026-09/02..11) are unusually thorough: between them they opened every section file of both papers, all P1 supplementary and bench files, the envelope and operational verifiers, the admission hook and its eight submodules, the kernel dispatch path, all seven Treaty Lean modules (with live #print axioms), the diff tests, the 20-case corpus, the replay-gate goldens, the specs, the claim registry, and the P1 revision plan's blocked-claims list. My own re-checks of the sections that drew no findings came back clean: P1 07-discussion and 10-conclusion carry no repo-checkable claim beyond restated macros; P1 02-background is accurate modulo XREF-05/22 and HARN-20; P1 03 struct field lists (TreatyScope, CrossKernelContinuation, ReceiptLineageStatement, ChioReceipt) match chio-runtime-core/src/types.rs L211-280 and chio-core-types/src/receipt/body.rs L42-103; "rejects a destructive class below receipt-backed" is real (chio-federation/src/treaty.rs L314-317); the bounded-predicate limits (64 KiB / 1 KiB / depth 32 / nodes 1,024, deny_unknown_fields everywhere) match treaty/predicate.rs L17-22; nine Lean atoms and nine receipt-view fields match ReceiptPredicate.lean; 1,024 proptest cases per property are real; all 38 manifest sourceFiles exist at HEAD; the hero-loop --producer-only / --packet-only modes match P1's producer/full description (packet-only = producer + `chio attest buyer verify-proof` + semantic checks); P1 Table 2's family-to-case mapping matches the corpus; P2's ten replay families match tests/replay/fixtures exactly (but are capability scenarios, as HARN-03/IMPL2-20 say). Live #print axioms: all four BilateralAccept theorems depend on [propext] only; both P1 theorems on [propext, Quot.sound], confirming FORM-01/HARN-04/PROSE-24 and P1's manifest.

CLAIM-CLASS COVERAGE. Production-enforced, bounded-theorem, differentially-aligned, and experimentally-measured classes are saturated. Two classes were thin and I filled them: (a) executable-demonstration claims about DENIAL artifacts (P2 says every denial is a signed canonical receipt / signed negative package; at HEAD envelope-level denials produce no receipt and the only "signed negative" outputs are five tampered workflow-receipt packages from chio-attest-loopback write_signed_negative_case_inputs) and (b) operational assumptions versus the repository's own registry (neither paper cites formal/assumptions.toml IDs; the canonical-JSON implementation in chio-core-types/src/canonical.rs had never been opened by any finder, and P2 attributes "Unicode string normalization" to RFC 8785, which neither the RFC nor the code performs). Smaller new items: the wire format does carry enforced per-signer and per-hash algorithm tags (KernelIdentity.alg == "ed25519", HashRecord.alg == "sha256") contrary to P2 09 L16; the selective-disclosure "issuer-owned key registry" is InMemoryIssuerRegistry documented for tests and fixtures; P2 calls BBS "group signatures" while the crate implements the CFRG BBS signature scheme; two P2 bib entries (RFC 9942, SCITT architecture now RFC 9943) are stale.

TEN MOST CONSEQUENTIAL CONFIRMED FINDINGS (ranked by how fast a hostile reader finds them and how much credibility each costs at launch):
1. BENCH1-01 + PROSE-07/08 + IMPL1-05/06 + BENCH1-02/03 (P1): the committed PDFs, CLAIM_LEDGER, abstract and Method section print 11.124 ms / 2.488 s and "Linux/aarch64 Neoverse-N1" while the retained results say 4.115 ms / 2.370 s on a Darwin MacBookPro. A numbers-versus-artifacts contradiction inside the paper's own directory is the single most damaging thing a reviewer can find in a paper whose thesis is "retained evidence".
2. IMPL2-01 + PROSE-03 + XREF-02 (P2): the gate-ordering claim ("signatures verify before G1-G6", "byte-level checks fire before state") is inverted at HEAD; Ed25519 verification is the last step of verify_chio_bilateral_dsse_envelope_inner and the operational verifier consults peer pins first. The paper's security argument rests on this order.
3. IMPL2-08/09 + PROSE-01/04 + XREF-03 (P2): the worked envelope, the "ten-field binding tuple", and subjectDigest = H(JCS(bindingTuple)) describe a wire format that does not exist; the real subject digest is SHA-256 of the canonical ChioReceipt body, and every predicate struct is deny_unknown_fields so the printed envelope would fail to decode.
4. IMPL2-05 + PROSE-02 + IMPL2-06 (P2): the "five rejection codes" taxonomy is not the code's taxonomy (16 VerifierError codes plus 8 BilateralCoSigningError codes; most envelope failures are CanonicalJson(String) distinguished by message prefix). The log2(5) oracle bound is derived from a taxonomy that is not shipped.
5. HARN-01 + IMPL2-16 + FORM-15 + XREF-06 (P2): "single-lane witness compromise" is defeated by a treaty-attached multi-lane witness quorum that exists only as a Lean LaneQuorumPolicy; Rust carries consistency_anchor: Option<String> and a single require/advisory witness bool.
6. HARN-02 + IMPL2-13 + XREF-05 (P2 vs P1): the "operator-resolution test parameterized by verifier-owned attribution metadata" does not exist; P1 records exactly this gap as non-testable assumption PS-A-01. The two papers contradict each other on what the deployed verifier checks.
7. XREF-01 + FORM-02 + FORM-01 + IMPL2-26 (P2): section 4 transcribes the May 2026 BilateralAccept.lean (receiptId, scope) that was replaced on 2026-07-12, and reports three kernel axioms where #print axioms shows [propext] only. The "audit artifact that pins the schema to a mechanical object" is itself out of date.
8. IMPL1-04 + BENCH1-04/06 (P1): scripts/generate-programmable-sovereignty-artifact.py --check fails at HEAD (Cargo.lock drift, 922 commits and 72 changed files under the covered crates since dfcd511651). The reproducibility promise on README L20-24 is currently false; the fix is a re-pin plus re-run, not prose.
9. PROSE-05 (P2, confirmed by web fetch in this wave and in 11-prose): bib key omegaTrustlets points arXiv 2605.03213 at "Omega: A TEE-Rooted Agentic Runtime" by Anonymous; the URL resolves to "When Agents Handle Secrets: A Survey of Confidential Computing for Agentic AI" (Forough, Kogias, Haddadi). A fabricated-looking citation is disqualifying at any venue.
10. IMPL2-18/19 + PROSE-34 + XREF-13 + IMPL2-17/PROSE-09 (P2): every number in section 6 (72.051 us on an "Apple M1 Max", the N=1/10/100 intersection sweep) has no retained artifact at HEAD, the 72.051 figure came from a kernel dispatch bench with no admission hook, no intersection runner ever existed, and section 5 discloses a "macOS Endpoint Security stub" that is not in the repository. Combined with BENCH1-09 (the cross-boundary allow row excludes the strict verify and SQLite write), the evaluation sections of both papers need to be regenerated from a single pinned run.

Practical consequence: P1 is close to defensible once numbers, environment, ledger, PDFs, the artifact pin, and the two ladder-mode and verifier-order wording issues are corrected; P2 is a May 2026 draft whose wire format, gate order, taxonomy, formal sketch, evaluation, and several attack claims no longer describe the repository and should be rewritten from P1's substrate rather than patched.

group_summaries.title: P1 implementation and evidence-pointer audit
group_summaries.summary: P1's implementation surface is real and hash-stable at HEAD (every manifest-listed source file, corpus, script and result file still matches its recorded sha256; only Cargo.lock and rust-toolchain.toml drift, and rust-toolchain.toml moved from 1.93.0 to 1.94.1 so the manifest's toolchain pin no longer matches the repo). All nine named symbols exist and behave as described in the main: the hook resolves everything from RuntimeAdmissionStores, treaty_ref_from_request denies a fixed key denylist, continuations are burned at admission and released on denial or abort, the deny benchmark drives a real ChioKernel with a counting tool server and asserts the counter per iteration, the bounded predicate limits are exactly 64 KiB / 1 KiB / 32 / 1024, the diff test enumerates nine atoms and runs proptest with cases=1024 for three properties within generator bounds, and the 20-case matrix runner checks an emitted code derived from the real error against expectedCode. The material problems are: (1) the fifth ladder mode is `maintenance` in spec/CHIO_LADDER.md and in both Rust ladder_mode_rank copies, not "quorum-required", and the two Rust copies disagree on a `quorum_required` alias; (2) verify_chio_bilateral_invocation, which section 5 presents as the receiver's bilateral-statement verifier with peer pins, live manifests and revocation-epoch checks, is called only by the offline buyer verifier; the pre-dispatch hook calls verify_chio_bilateral_dsse_envelope plus its own binding checks and never consults a peer pin set, ladder-manifest freshness, revocation oracle, lease registry or receipt store; (3) the claim that matrix "envelope cases call the strict verifier; store and policy cases call the admission hook" is false for six of twenty cases (PS-TH-01..03 call pure runtime-core functions; PS-TH-13/14/19 call verify_bilateral_cosign_invocation, which the code documents as a partial, non-conformant verifier); (4) CLAIM_LEDGER.md's latency numbers contradict the hash-pinned bench JSON, and the section 6 hardware description contradicts the hash-pinned environment file. Several smaller precision issues (revocation records not in the denylist, no distinct reserve-then-consume transition, error-code attribution, admission-report digest is substituted not compared, budget charge after the hook, in-memory admission store in the deny benchmark) are listed with the true behavior at HEAD.

group_summaries.title: P1 measurement and reproducibility audit
group_summaries.summary: P1's numbers are internally split across two benchmark runs. Every prose number, the committed PDFs, and CLAIM_LEDGER.md come from a 2026-07-26 run on this Linux Neoverse-N1 workstation (the "eight-core Arm server ... 49.2 GB" of the abstract and section 6), while the retained result files at HEAD (bench/results/*.json, *.csv, *-inline.tex, committed 2026-08-01 by Codex at 0c01448309, producer commit 3dfd241e67) come from a MacBook Pro (aarch64-apple-darwin, T6000) and are 1.4x to 4.3x faster per component. The TeX sources would typeset the Mac numbers under Linux prose; the committed paper.pdf and paper-usenix.pdf (built 2026-07-26 20:22 EDT, pdfTeX TeX Live 2023/Debian) still print the Linux numbers; CLAIM_LEDGER.md prints the Linux numbers. The artifact manifest pins sha256 of the stale PDF, the stale ledger, and the new results together and never cross-checks them, so the "check passes" notion is hollow; at HEAD it fails anyway on Cargo.lock and rust-toolchain.toml (1.93.0 pinned, 1.94.1 at HEAD), which also makes --full unrunnable from its first line. Methodologically: all p99 values are literally the maximum sample (index ceil(0.99n)-1 = n-1 for n=20 and n=30); Criterion "samples" are batch means over 1..30 iterations; no mean, CI, variance, or outlier count is reported although Criterion produced them (July log shows a +46% run-to-run swing on strict_bilateral_dsse_verify); the Aug 1 run retained no Criterion log at all. The full-hook allow path, throughput, and store growth are not measured; cross_boundary_admission_allow (14 us) is a pure function over pre-verified evidence flags. The scripts, benches, negative-corpus test names, CLI subcommands, and replay-gate crate all exist at HEAD and do what section 6 describes (2 warmups, 20/30 samples, release profile, dispatch counter, SQLite denial receipt), but the admission store in the deny benchmark is InMemoryRuntimeAdmissionStore (only the receipt store is SQLite), and the 10.7 s / 11 s matrix timings are dominated by 20 cargo invocations.

group_summaries.title: P2 implementation-claim audit
group_summaries.summary: P2 (bilateral-receipt-admission) is a 2026-05-18 draft whose implementation claims describe a verifier, wire format, trust store, rejection taxonomy, anchor policy, and benchmark set that do not exist at HEAD fe5657020c in the form stated. Blockers: (1) gate order is inverted, Ed25519 signatures are verified LAST in verify_chio_bilateral_dsse_envelope_inner and the operational verifier consults the peer pin set before any byte-level check; (2) the "five rejection codes" are not wire strings anywhere in crates or spec (real taxonomy: 16 VerifierError codes plus 8 BilateralCoSigningError codes), and the bilateral_dsse.rs:996 citation points at a 100-line module shim; (3) the worked envelope and "ten-field binding tuple" use camelCase fields, lease {epoch, expiry}, signerKids, leaseHash, signerKidsHash that appear nowhere, and every predicate struct is deny_unknown_fields so the printed envelope would fail decode; (4) the subject digest is SHA-256 of the canonical ChioReceipt body (spec section 4, receipt_body_digest_hex, cosign.rs L195-215), not H(JCS(bindingTuple)), and the strict envelope verifier does not check the digest at all; (5) no treaty multi-lane witness quorum exists in Rust (TreatyScope has no lane field, WitnessPolicy is a single require/advisory bool, AnchorBatchBody carries one witness; the Lean LaneQuorumPolicy has no Rust mirror). Majors: asymmetric IssuerKeys/KernelKeys store exists only in Lean; operator-attribution metadata for signer reuse does not exist; BBS stub-vs-real is a chio-selective-disclosure schema check unrelated to the bilateral verifier; the macOS Endpoint Security stub is not in the repo; 72.051 us and the N=1/10/100 intersection numbers came from bench result files deleted 2026-07-26 with no generator for the intersection sweep even at authoring; the 50-fixture replay corpus is real but its families are kernel-capability scenarios misdescribed as bilateral DSSE gates; the "three denial fixtures" map to different codes in a 20-case corpus; the lease gate has no epoch and runs after the digest gate; BilateralAccept.lean no longer has receiptId and depends only on propext; "no live cross-process federation" is stale given chio-federation-transport-iroh; and the federated-origin fail-closed path keys off a request field no production adapter sets. Positive: the 50-golden replay gate, the strict_bilateral_dsse_verify bench, the iroh lane, and the Ed25519-authoritative / BBS-secondary posture are real at HEAD.

group_summaries.title: Formal-claims audit for both papers (Lean)
group_summaries.summary: Formal-statement audit of both whitepapers against the Lean Treaty lane at HEAD fe5657020c. P1 (programmable-sovereignty) is formally honest: its two cited theorems finite_refinement_sound / finite_refinement_exact exist in ReceiptPredicate.lean, carry exactly the axioms the paper and its supplementary manifest claim ([propext, Quot.sound], no project axioms), the file hash matches the artifact manifest, and the paper's notation (syntax, nine atoms, nine-field receipt view, admits, refinesOn, theorem statement) matches the Lean line for line. Its depth is a shallow List.all characterization, which P1 does not oversell. Its gaps are institutional: ReceiptPredicate.lean is absent from formal/proof-manifest.toml's root file list, formal/theorem-inventory.json, and the Lean mutation allowlist, so nothing in the repo's own claim discipline tracks P1's theorems. P2 (bilateral-receipt-admission) has material formal problems: (1) it misreports the axiom footprint (#print axioms gives [propext] only for freestanding_accept_set_theorem and all three corollaries; the paper says propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound); (2) its description of the Lean objects is stale (envelope carries an AdmissionView, not a receipt id; TrustStore has no LeaseEpoch); (3) it calls a definitional bi-conditional "load-bearing" and "no hidden side channel" in section 1 and the README while section 4 says it is not load-bearing; (4) the "six runtime gates collapse into three" claim has no Lean or Rust artifact, the Lean trust store is asymmetric while the Rust verifier is symmetric, and signatures are verified last in Rust; (5) the abstract says six gates over canonical bytes are formalized in Lean, but Lean formalizes three conjuncts and never inspects bytes; (6) essential_preserved_chain is misdescribed as characterizing amendment as backward refinement, when it is a list-indexed induction principle whose per-step preservation is a hypothesis and whose admitsEssential relation runs in the opposite direction; (7) the polity theorems P2 leans on are definitional (amendment_admissible_iff_backward_refinement is Iff.rfl; ratchet_attack_requires_dropping_essential and meta_amendment_requires_dropping_designated are propositional tautologies; treaty_admission_iff_predicate_intersection is Bool.and_assoc); (8) the anchor lane quorum model P2's section 7 invokes is rfl-level Lean with no Rust counterpart. Mutation evidence: six of the twelve open Lean survivors (#1005 to #1010) are in PredicateLang's supported/defined, and I verified in Lean that survivor #1007 alone lets an unavailable-mode atom become an allow via neg (disj _ bot), a shape no theorem in the tree covers; #1010 is provably equivalent w.r.t. denote. No Aeneas extraction exists for any treaty function; the mirror anchors are explicitly "drift tripwires, not a Rust refinement proof".

group_summaries.title: Formal harness and evidence-estate audit (what exists beyond Lean, and what the papers miss)
group_summaries.summary: Harness-estate review of P1 (programmable-sovereignty) and P2 (bilateral-receipt-admission) at HEAD fe5657020c. The bilateral/treaty/continuation path has NO Kani harness (zero #[kani::proof] in chio-federation and chio-runtime-core), no Creusot contract, no fuzz target (federation_trust_establishment covers the handshake, not DSSE), and sits outside the cargo-mutants scope (6 crates, neither federation nor runtime-core) and outside the spec/proof mutation registries. Its formal evidence is: Lean Treaty modules (PredicateLang theorems with [[mirror]] hash tripwires; BilateralAccept definitional theorem; ReceiptPredicate, which is root-imported but NOT registered in formal/proof-manifest.toml root_modules or formal/theorem-inventory.json), Apalache PostAdmissionDropGuard (RetainedIffAborted, ReservationConservation) and ReceiptBeforeAllow with mirror anchors on ChioRuntimeAdmissionHook::release_reservations/release_reserved and record_chio_receipt_with_federation, and a large uncited runtime-test estate: c2_bilateral_invocation_partial_verifier.rs (24 byte-mutation tests mapped to spec 7.1 codes), b4 DSSE/PAE conformance (17 tests), a generated bilateral_dsse_producer state machine, kernel federation_cosign.rs (forged treaty metadata cannot reach dispatch or cosign; unpinned peer fails closed pre-dispatch; cosigner not called when persistence fails), and runtime_kernel_hook.rs fail-closed tests. Neither paper cites any of these. Two P2 claims describe gates that do not exist in Rust (multi-lane witness quorum on a treaty; operator-resolution of keyids via attribution metadata), P2 mischaracterizes the 50-fixture replay corpus (it is the kernel capability golden gate, not DSSE), P2's axiom footprint is wrong (#print axioms gives [propext] only), and P2's rejection-code bit bound rests on a fictional five-code taxonomy. P1 is far more disciplined; its gaps are ordering (budget admission runs after the treaty hook, not before), the fifth ladder mode name, an unregistered Lean module, and assumption-table omissions (ASSUME-OS-CLOCK, ASSUME-SQLITE-ATOMICITY, ASSUME-SUBPROCESS-ISOLATION, canonical-JSON scope, and the unregistered but load-bearing federated-origin classification assumption). Continuation single-use is store-enforced (SQLite PRIMARY KEY continuation_id, INSERT OR IGNORE) and tested single-process, but has no crash, Loom, or per-identifier model; release on denial is best-effort and the kernel retains fail-closed on failure, so P2's "released back to free" is an overclaim.

group_summaries.title: Cross-paper consistency, six-paper family, and spec alignment
group_summaries.summary: Cross-paper and spec-alignment audit of P1 (programmable-sovereignty, HEAD title "Receiver-Owned Bilateral Admission...") and P2 (bilateral-receipt-admission) against the four sibling papers and spec/CHIO_BILATERAL_COSIGN_INVOCATION.md, CHIO_LADDER.md, CHIO_SELECTIVE_DISCLOSURE.md, PROTOCOL.md, the Lean Treaty modules, and the Rust verifier at HEAD fe5657020c. Verdict: the two papers describe the same construction (predicate chio.bilateral-cosign-invocation.v1, verify_chio_bilateral_dsse_envelope, the pre-dispatch hook, the three-vendor closure) and claim the same gap, but disagree on almost every checkable detail: gate count and order, rejection-code taxonomy, key-role model (symmetric vs issuer/kernel), what the subject digest binds (receipt body vs a ten-field tuple), which Lean module carries the claim and what it says (P2 misstates BilateralAccept's input type, axioms, and dependencies), the threat model on one-actor-two-keys (P2 contradicts itself and P1), the role of BBS and anchors (absent from P1, load-bearing in P2 with a treaty witness policy that does not exist), vocabulary (P1 has zero uses of "polity" and disclaims sovereignty; P2 uses polity 22 times and cites a "polity-layer construction" that is the pre-2026-07-26 version of P1 itself), and benchmarks (P2 declares measurements out of scope that P1 reports). P2 is an older draft (last commit 2026-06-09) that predates both the crate move and the P1 refocus; P1 is accurate against HEAD on every point I could check except the fifth ladder-mode name. The family-wide ladder mode set is inconsistent across spec (maintenance), federation Rust (maintenance), runtime-core Rust (maintenance or quorum_required aliased), Lean (quorumRequired), and P1 (quorum-required). The cosign spec is stale against code in four places (two predicate URIs vs one accepted; two spec-only error codes and three code-only codes; n_of_m signature count; verification step order). Recommendation: P1 survives; retire P2 and merge four specific paragraphs into P1 after rewriting them against the real code.

The sensor-grounded paper's bib.bib L175-L179 cites the parent under a third title ('Programmable Sovereignty: A Predicate-Conditioned Polity Substrate with Bilateral Treaty Composition', author Chio Project, year 2027), so the family cites the parent under three different titles, none of which is P1's HEAD title.

group_summaries.title: Prose, structure, and reader-experience audit
group_summaries.summary:
Reader-experience verdict. P1 (Receiver-Owned Bilateral Admission) reads as a competent, honest systems paper: the reader knows WHAT by abstract sentence 3 and intro paragraph 2, WHY by the refund example in intro paragraph 1, and is lost only in section 3.1 (noun-list walls: TreatyScope names 8 things, the predicate paragraph names 12) and in section 4, which presents the Lean model before the reader learns (5.4) that it is "not an alternate authorization path". Its problem is the opposite of P2's: 18% of sentences hedge (intro 32%), the "two keys are not two organizations" disclaimer appears nine times and the "Lean does not verify Rust" disclaimer four times in the body plus README, CLAIM_LEDGER and supplementary README, and the introduction ends on a disclaimer. The contribution does not disappear, but the paper reads as a rebuttal to a previous review rather than a foundational document. Two factual defects survive: the fifth ladder mode is named "quorum-required" (HEAD: maintenance), and the CLAIM_LEDGER and prose environment disagree with the paper's own retained result files. Four floats, including the main results table, are never referenced.

P2 (Bilateral Receipt Admission) is not submittable in its current form. Its spine, "five rejection codes", does not exist at HEAD (16 VerifierError codes plus BilateralCoSigningError codes, none with the paper's names). The "binding tuple" has five different cardinalities across abstract (7), section 3 opening (12), "ten-field tuple" prose, fig:envelope (9 boxes, caption says ten, Description enumerates nine), and the worked envelope (11 keys), and the worked envelope's "_type" string would be rejected by the shipped verifier. Section 3 says signatures verify before G1-G6; section 6 says canonical checks run before any signature check; HEAD verifies signatures last. A cited reference (omegaTrustlets, arXiv 2605.03213) points at a different paper. The section-5 macOS Endpoint Security paragraph describes an integration that does not exist. The reader understands WHAT only at section 3's binding-tuple paragraph, never gets a concrete WHY (no scenario), and is lost in section 4 (six gates collapse to three with self-contradicting justification), section 6 (measures the local-policy path, not the construction), and the fourteen "anonymized for review" deferrals. 43 sentences exceed 40 words (max 115); "structural(ly)" 15x, "load-bearing" 6x, "rather than" 25x. Both papers omit Macaroons, Biscuit, UCAN, SPIFFE/SPIRE, RFC 8693, VC/VP, PolicyMaker/KeyNote, SDSI/SPKI, Kerberos cross-realm, BeyondCorp, AWS cross-account policy, MCP/A2A (the repo ships chio-mcp-edge and chio-a2a-adapter), and x402/AP2.

Adjacent facts the finder missed:
1. The runtime hook discards the verifier error: crates/kernel/chio-runtime-core/src/admission_hook/dsse.rs L121-129 maps every verify_chio_bilateral_dsse_envelope failure to the single code chio_treaty_unverified_required_evidence with a fixed detail string. At the runtime protocol surface there is ONE envelope-failure code, not five and not sixteen. This cuts against PROSE-02, PROSE-11 and PROSE-25 in both directions: library errors are finer (values echoed), runtime denials are coarser (one code).
2. P2 05 L10's ordering claim ('every byte-level check fires before the verifier consults state the sender cannot see') is false for the operational verifier: cosign.rs consults peer_pin_set (L60-95) before the canonical-bytes, keyid-distinctness and signature checks run inside verify_chio_bilateral_dsse_envelope (called at L108-117).
3. P2's worked envelope fails at serde decode (deny_unknown_fields on DsseStatement, StatementSubject, BilateralPredicate; required fields missing), before the _type gate. The spec's own section 4 example uses predicateType 'https://in-toto.io/attestation/bilateral-cosign-invocation/v1', which the shipped verifier also rejects (it checks the literal 'chio.bilateral-cosign-invocation.v1'); so the spec example and the code disagree on the predicate type URI, and PROSE-04's suggested fallback to the spec example would not verify either.
4. Spec section 7.1 lists 15 codes and VerifierError has 16; they are not the same set. Spec-only: consistency.anchor_unverified, consistency.quorum_underpopulated. Code-only: ladder.manifest_missing, ladder.manifest_stale, governance.unknown_action_class. Any 'regenerate the taxonomy from the spec' fix must pick one source.
5. No treaty-bound multi-lane witness quorum exists in Rust: chio-anchor WitnessPolicy is a single require_public_witness bool plus a stale window (witness.rs L244-254), and chio-anchor is not a dependency of chio-federation, chio-runtime-core or chio-kernel. LaneQuorumPolicy exists only in Lean (PredicateLang.lean L540-575). P2 07 L10 'the treaty's declared multi-lane witness policy' describes nothing shipped.
6. The runtime-core ladder_mode_rank accepts 'quorum_required' as a legacy alias of maintenance at rank 4 (treaty.rs L758) and the proof-manifest mirror covers that runtime-core function, not the federation one. P1's 'quorum-required' is therefore an alias spelled as the consistency-model value, not a pure invention.
7. docs/papers/reversible-action/sections/06-evaluation.tex L105-108 makes the same macOS Endpoint Security stub claim as P2 05 L33 ('the entitlement is declared, the class is structurally present'); zero matching files exist outside docs/ at HEAD. That sibling paper is outside this wave but the lead should know the claim propagates.
8. Finder line numbers are unreliable for P2 sections 05, 07, 09 and P1 sections 02, 04, 08, 09 (they cite lines beyond the files' lengths). Every quoted sentence was found at the corrected lines given in the evidence fields; no finding was refuted on that basis.
